mcq.q: B is the wife of A. A is the father of G. How is B related to G?
mcq.explain: Draw the tree one statement at a time (B is the wife of A; A is the father of G), marking males and females. Then trace from G back to B: B is G's mother. Convention: brothers and sisters share both parents, and a parent's husband or wife is also a parent (no step-relations).
mcq.fast: Draw the tree with + for male and − for female; follow the chain from G to B.

mcq.q: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Vivek said, "He is the brother of my daughter." How is that man related to Vivek?
mcq.explain: Start from the speaker ("my") and move one word at a time: daughter → brother. Following these links on a small family tree lands on son, so the person in the photograph is Vivek's son. Convention: brothers and sisters share both parents, and a parent's husband or wife is also a parent (no step-relations).
mcq.fast: Read the possessive chain from "my" outward and simplify two words at a time (father's wife = mother, mother's brother = uncle …).

mcq.q: In a code, X + Y says "X is the father of Y"; X @ Y says "X is the daughter of Y"; X − Y says "X is the brother of Y"; X × Y says "X is the mother of Y". If G − C × D @ J, how is G related to J?
mcq.explain: Decode left to right: G is the brother of C; C is the mother of D; D is the daughter of J. Drawing these links gives: G is J's brother-in-law. Convention: brothers and sisters share both parents, and a parent's husband or wife is also a parent (no step-relations).
mcq.fast: Translate each symbol into words first, draw the three links, then read the asked relation.

mcq.q: Your mother's father is your:
mcq.explain: Relatives on the father's side are "paternal" and on the mother's side "maternal". Your mother's father is on your mother's side, so the relation is maternal grandfather. The word after paternal/maternal follows the generation and gender: brother → uncle, sister → aunt, parents → grandparents.
